prompt:
Create an exact 3-by-3 pixel-art atlas from the supplied source grid. Each cell must be the complete same 64×29 lower-half portrait crop (overall aspect ratio 64:29), with original jaw, chin, nose, neck, hair and background registration unchanged. No labels, gutters, borders or extra panels. Place mouth poses in row-major order A B C / D E F / G H X.

Keep this character's angry mood restrained and readable through firmer source-colored lips and slight nose-bridge tension, without extreme downturned corners or an exaggerated smile. Preserve original lip scale and center, warm brown/terracotta palette, skin tone, jaw and all crop alignment. For any visible teeth use muted neutral ivory/gray, clearly distinct from skin; avoid tooth gaps, skin-colored teeth, bright shiny teeth, lipstick-red lips, thick black outlines or large patches of changed surrounding skin. Pixel-art edges stay crisp and naturally stepped.

Use these Rhubarb mouth-shape meanings exactly:
A: pressured closed P/B/M.
B: narrow opening, teeth nearly together, consonants/EE.
C: medium unrounded EH/AE.
D: wide AA.
E: slightly rounded AO/ER, no wider than C.
F: puckered UW/OW/W.
G: upper teeth touching lower lip, F/V.
H: tongue raised behind upper teeth for L, opening between C and D.
X: relaxed closed idle.

Maintain each pose's phoneme meaning and clear differences between poses. Angry A/X may carry the firmer emotional lip set; do not let the expression erase the phoneme pose. Avoid a giant grin across the atlas.
